d: Orphaned as a baby, this boy grew up in a cupboard under the stairs before learning he was famous in a world he had never heard of. He carries a lightning-shaped scar.

job: Student, later joke-shop owner and Auror
d: The sixth of seven children, he grew up with hand-me-down robes and a rat for a pet. Spiders terrify him, and he plays Keeper for his house team.
The brightest witch of her age, born to two dentists. She used a Time-Turner to take extra classes and founded a society for the welfare of house-elves.
Known for defeating a dark wizard in 1945, he loves sherbet lemons and wears half-moon spectacles. He owns a phoenix.
Raised in a Muggle orphanage, he became the most feared dark wizard of all time and split his soul to cheat death.
A sallow, greasy-haired teacher who spent years coveting the Defence Against the Dark Arts post. His childhood friendship with a Muggle-born girl shaped his whole life.
A pale, pointed-faced pure-blood who sneers at anyone he thinks is beneath him. In his sixth year he was given a task he couldn't bring himself to finish.
A wealthy pure-blood with long blond hair and a snake-headed cane. He slipped a dangerous old diary into a cauldron at Flourish and Blotts.
A blonde pure-blood witch who once lied to the Dark Lord's face to protect her son.
A shabby, kind teacher with a secret that comes out once a month. He taught his class to fight boggarts by laughing at them.
He spent twelve years in Azkaban for a crime he did not commit and escaped by slipping past the guards in animal form.
A small, watery-eyed wizard who faked his own death by cutting off a finger and lived for years as a family pet.
A stern witch in emerald robes who can turn into a tabby cat. She is head of the lions' house.
A forgetful boy raised by his formidable grandmother. He's gifted with plants and once pulled a sword from a hat in front of the Dark Lord.
A dreamy girl who wears radish earrings and a butterbeer-cork necklace, and believes firmly in Crumple-Horned Snorkacks.

job: Student, later Quidditch player and journalist
d: The only girl among seven siblings, she was possessed through an old diary in her first year and became a fierce Chaser.
One half of a pair of mischief-making twins who left school in a burst of fireworks to open a shop in Diagon Alley.
A prankster twin who lost an ear to a curse during an escape from Privet Drive.
A pompous Prefect and Head Boy who wrote a report on cauldron bottoms and sided with the Ministry over his own family.
A cool, ponytailed eldest son with a fang earring who works with tombs in Egypt. A werewolf's attack left him scarred.
A stocky, freckled former Seeker who works with dragons in Romania.

job: Ministry of Magic, Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office
d: A balding Ministry wizard fascinated by Muggles. He enchanted a Ford Anglia to fly and collects plugs.
A plump, fierce mother of seven who knits jumpers for everyone and keeps a clock showing where each family member is.

job: Gamekeeper, Care of Magical Creatures teacher
d: A half-giant who was expelled in his third year. He dreams of owning a dragon and keeps a pink umbrella that hides something.
A toad-like witch in fluffy pink cardigans who decorates her office with kitten plates and makes students write lines in their own blood.

job: Author, Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher
d: A vain, golden-haired author who took credit for other wizards' deeds and erased their memories. Winner of Witch Weekly's Most-Charming-Smile Award five times.

job: Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher
d: A nervous, stuttering teacher who always wears a turban and smells oddly of garlic.
A paranoid retired Auror with a wooden leg and a magical eye that can see through walls. He only drinks from his own hip flask.
A heavy-lidded witch with wild dark hair, devoted to the Dark Lord. She tortured a pair of Aurors into madness.
A clumsy young Auror who can change her appearance at will and likes her hair bubblegum pink. Don't call her by her first name.
A house-elf with tennis-ball eyes who punishes himself, wears mismatched socks, and was freed by a sock hidden in a diary.
A bitter old house-elf who mutters insults under his breath and treasures a locket left by his young master.
A house-elf who took her dismissal so hard she drowned her sorrows in butterbeer in the Hogwarts kitchens.
A handsome Hufflepuff Seeker and Prefect who became a champion for his school. He was told to share a cup.
A pretty Ravenclaw Seeker who cried a lot in the year after her boyfriend died.
A surly, hook-nosed international Seeker who walks like a duck and invited a bookish girl to the Yule Ball.
Part-Veela, she was her school's champion and later married into a large red-haired family.
A thin, bespectacled seer draped in shawls who predicts a student's death every year. Twice in her life she gave a real prophecy.
A squat witch with flyaway grey hair and earth on her clothes. She runs the greenhouses and heads the badger house.
A tiny teacher who has to stand on a pile of books to see over his desk. He was once a duelling champion.
A bad-tempered Squib caretaker who longs to hang students by their thumbs and adores his cat.
A strict school nurse who can regrow bones overnight but never lets visitors stay long.
A spotty, gloomy ghost who haunts a girls' bathroom on the first floor. She died after seeing a pair of yellow eyes.
A troublemaking poltergeist who drops water balloons, sings rude songs, and only obeys the Bloody Baron.

who: Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington (Nearly Headless Nick)
d: A ghost whose execution went badly: forty-five chops with a blunt axe left his head hanging by a thread. He holds a Deathday party.
A spoilt Muggle boy who was given a pig's tail and later became a boxing champion.
A beefy, purple-faced Muggle with a huge moustache who sells drills and hates anything unusual.
A bony Muggle woman with a long neck, perfect for spying on the neighbours. She was jealous of her magical sister.
A portly politician in a lime-green bowler hat who refused to believe the Dark Lord had returned.
A tall, bald wizard with a deep, slow voice and a single gold earring. He guarded a Muggle Prime Minister while undercover.
A small, smelly, droopy-eyed thief who sold off treasures from Grimmauld Place.
A Death Eater smuggled out of Azkaban by his own family and later spent a whole year disguised as someone else.

job: Head of the Department of International Magical Cooperation
d: A rigid Ministry official with a toothbrush moustache who sent his own son to Azkaban and could speak over two hundred languages.

job: Head of the Department of Magical Games and Sports
d: A former Beater with a broken nose who bet heavily on the Quidditch World Cup and ran from goblin debts.
A gossip writer with jewelled spectacles and a Quick-Quotes Quill, who is secretly an unregistered beetle Animagus.
A soft-voiced wandmaker with pale silvery eyes who remembers every wand he has ever sold.
A golden-haired dark wizard who wanted wizards to rule 'for the greater good'. He stole a legendary wand from a wandmaker's workshop.
A grumpy barman who smells of goats. He resented his famous brother for years.
A savage werewolf who attacks children on purpose and wears Death Eater robes without being given the Mark.
A Muggle-born first-year who followed a famous classmate with his camera, asking for signed photos.
An Irish half-blood whose attempts at magic have a habit of blowing up in his face.
A giggling Divination fan who called her sixth-year boyfriend 'Won-Won'.
A burly Quidditch captain so obsessed with winning the Cup that he once had a dream about it.
A sixteen-foot-tall half-brother brought back from the mountains and tied up in the Forbidden Forest.
A goblin who led a first-year down to his vault and later helped rob Gringotts, for a price.
A palomino centaur with white-blond hair who let a human ride on his back and was cast out of his herd.
A younger brother who joined the Death Eaters, then turned against them and stole a locket from a cave.
The author of Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, a set textbook at Hogwarts.
A huge, slow-witted boy with very long arms who follows a pale classmate everywhere.
A tall Gryffindor who supports West Ham and is good at drawing. He was briefly on the run with a goblin.
A tall, thin headmaster with a goatee who gave up names to escape Azkaban.
A very large and elegant headmistress who swears she simply has big bones.
A lion-like former Auror who became Minister and wanted the 'Chosen One' as a poster boy.
A violent, bedraggled pure-blood who lived in squalor and wore a ring he claimed came from the Peverells.
A downtrodden witch who used a love potion on a Muggle neighbour and died after giving birth in an orphanage.
